title: Diagram
description:
A Diagram, in version 1 of the JSON model that @the-platform/diagrams reads. A tool that generates Diagrams can check its output against this schema, then default-export the JSON from a `<name>.diagram.ts` module, where the Diagram joins the Atlas like any other.

A Diagram's Notation decides which Kinds and statuses its Nodes, Groups and Edges may have, and which fields. The schema checks each Diagram against its own Notation's.

A model that fails this schema fails the engine's validation too. But passing this schema doesn't make a Diagram valid. Some rules relate one part of the model to another, which JSON Schema can't express. The engine's validation checks them, and reports each under its rule's name:

- `duplicate-id`: Node and Group ids are unique within a Diagram, in one namespace, and each Edge id is unique among its Edges.
- `duplicate-row`: the Rows of one Node have names of their own, since an Edge end names a Row by its name.
- `edge-end`: each Edge end names a Node on the Diagram, never a Group, and an end at a Row names one of that Node's Rows.
- `edge-end-kind`: each Edge starts and ends at Nodes of Kinds that its own Kind may join.
- `nesting`: each member names a Node or a Group on the Diagram, every Node and Group is a member of exactly one parent, the Diagram or one Group, and so Groups nest as a tree.
- `default-edge-id`: an Edge whose id is its default name, its two Nodes' ids joined by `->`, keeps it only while no other Edge joins the same two Nodes.

`diagrams lint` checks the Atlas as a whole too:

- `kind-conflict` and `title-conflict`: an id names one thing across the Atlas, with one Kind and one title on every Diagram that draws it, as a Node or as a Group.
- `broken-link`: every Link resolves, to an id that some Diagram draws, or to a file inside the repo and, with a `section`, to one of its headings.

version.description: The version of the JSON model. This engine reads version 1.

notation.description: The Notation the Diagram is written in, which decides the Kinds, statuses and fields that its Nodes, Groups and Edges may have.

id.description: The path of the Diagram's module from the repo root, minus `.diagram.ts`, such as `docs/shop`. The Atlas sets it, so a generated Diagram can leave it out.

description.description: What the Diagram shows, which isn't drawn. The SVG carries it in its model.

direction.description: Which way the ranks run: `right`, the default, or `down`.

members.description: The ids of the Diagram's top-level Nodes and Groups, in declaration order, which breaks layout ties.

nodes.description: Every Node on the Diagram, whatever its Group.

groups.description: Every Group on the Diagram, whatever its parent.

walkthroughs.description: The Diagram's Walkthroughs. This engine doesn't play them yet, so the list must be empty.

id.description: Lowercase kebab-case words, such as `payments-api`, optionally namespaced by a context, as in `billing/order`.

text.description: Text that an SVG can hold. XML forbids some characters even written as character references, so no SVG can hold them: the control characters from U+0000 to U+001F other than tab, line feed and carriage return; halves of surrogate pairs on their own, from U+D800 to U+DFFF; and U+FFFE and U+FFFF. The engine reports them as `invalid-character`.

someText.description: Text with something in it other than spaces, tabs and line breaks.

technology.description: The slug of the product, language or protocol it's built with: lowercase words joined by hyphens, such as `postgres` or `grpc`. Any slug is valid. One without a logo is drawn as its name.

row.description: A name and a value shown on a Node, such as `replicas: 3`. Every Row has a Port on each side of its Node.

name.description: The Row's name, drawn on the left. An Edge end names a Row by it.

value.description: The Row's value, drawn on the right. A number is written as a string, such as `"3"`.

end.description: An Edge end: the id of a Node, whose header Port the Edge uses, or one of the Node's Rows, whose Port on the matching side it uses instead.

rowEnd.description: An Edge end at one of a Node's Rows.

link.description: A "see also" pointer from a Node or a Group to exactly one thing: another id, or a Markdown document.

idLink.description: A Link to another id in the Atlas.

id.description: The id it leads to, which some Diagram in the Atlas draws.

label.description: Replaces the text shown for the Link.

docLink.description: A Link to a Markdown document, such as an ADR or a spec, and optionally to one of its sections.

doc.description: The document's path from the repo root, such as `docs/adr/0001-clean-room.md`.

section.description: A heading in the document, by its text or by its anchor.

label.description: Replaces the text shown for the Link.

architecture.description: What a Diagram of the architecture Notation holds: Nodes, Groups and Edges of the Kinds that the Notation has, each with the fields that its Diagrams may have.

node.description: One thing drawn on a Diagram of the architecture Notation.

id.description: The Node's id, which names one thing across the Atlas: it has one Kind and one title on every Diagram.

kind.description: The Node's Kind, which alone decides how it looks.

title.description: The Node's title, drawn in its header. A title too wide for its Kind is shortened.

technology.description: What the Node is built with, drawn in its header.

external.description: Whether the Node stands for something we don't own or run, drawn with a dashed outline.

status.description: How the Node is doing, shown as a mark at the end of its header.

rows.description: The Node's Rows, drawn below its header, one band each, in order.

description.description: What the Node is, which isn't drawn. The SVG carries it in its model.

callout.description: A short tag above the Node that draws attention to it, such as `single point of failure`.

group.description: A labeled box drawn around Nodes and other Groups, on a Diagram of the architecture Notation.

id.description: The Group's id, which names one thing across the Atlas: it has one Kind and one title on every Diagram.

kind.description: The Group's Kind, which alone decides how it looks.

title.description: The Group's title, drawn in its label band.

members.description: The ids of the Group's Nodes and child Groups, in declaration order.

description.description: What the Group is, which isn't drawn.

edge.description: A connection from one Port to another, on a Diagram of the architecture Notation.

id.description: An id, or the Edge's default name: its two Nodes' ids joined by `->`, as in `checkout-api->payments-api`.

kind.description: The Edge's Kind, which alone decides how it looks.

label.description: What passes over the Edge, drawn beside it, such as `Places orders`.

technology.description: How it travels, drawn below the label.

rate.description: How much passes over it, drawn below the label: a number, an optional `k` or `M`, a slash, and `s`, `min` or `h`, as in `2k/s` or `30/min`.
